species.name: Chicken
species.summary: The best-documented animal in the current build. Buy from Angela, keep hay and water in the coop trough, mount the coop heater on the outside wall, and pet daily for a shot at large eggs.
species.searchTags: chicken hen rooster chick poultry coop egg large egg hay heater angela gigi quest food diet feed price buy sell

facts.text: Buy chickens from Angela, the chicken seller NPC. After purchase they do not enter your backpack — they appear in the small fenced field behind her house. Grab them manually: carry them home one by one on foot, or load them into a car boot.
In every documented case the coop-mission stuck point came from missing the post-purchase prompt; other bugs in this mission cannot be ruled out.
Exact chicken purchase price is unverified. One player reported about 4,000+C for four chickens; treat as a lead only.
Chickens live in a coop. The heater and AC must be the coop/barn versions bought from Angela — the house decoration heater/AC sold at City Hall does nothing for coops.
Mount the coop heater on the outside of the coop exterior wall.
A fenced outdoor roaming area matters: chickens that can roam outside in an enclosed area get the chance to lay large eggs.
Chicks exist as the early growth stage of chickens; 2 additional rooster variations were added.
Chickens eat hay — they pick the grains out of hay/straw piles.
Two ways to feed: hold hay near the animal to hand-feed (raises the food reserve bar in its info tab), or fill the trough and animals eat by themselves once every morning, covering the whole day.
General daily care: only the trough inside the coop needs filling — animals eat and drink inside before leaving in the morning, so outdoor troughs stay optional while the door is open.
Hay comes from cutting bushes or looting crates and barrels on NPC farms.
Water is supplied through a trough; hand-feeding does not work for water — the water reserve bar only refills from a trough.
For automated water, a water tower alone is not enough — you must sign a water contract with the mayor at City Hall, then the tower refills on its own.

Adult chickens with every need and satisfaction maxed start laying. Egg size (S/M/L) and whether an egg is fertile are RNG; hover an egg to check fertility. Large eggs are the rarest and require maxed needs plus happiness.
Chicken Egg - Small retails at 60C on the Leafy Market shelf. This is a shop purchase price, not what your eggs sell for.
Chicken Breast and Chicken Leg exist as current-build shop items, confirming the meat path for culled chickens.
Meat, milk and eggs are species-specific items.
An egg-hatching mechanic for oviparous animals is documented.
Large eggs arrived only around the 4th-5th batch for one player — pure RNG; daily petting raises the animal rating and large eggs became noticeably more frequent.
An animal sickness mechanic exists; the heater prevents temperature sickness but cannot cure an already sick animal.
Take sick chickens to the veterinarian. The vet only treats animals that are actually sick — a famished (starving) animal is turned away.
A famished chicken recovers by the next morning if you bring it back to the coop and feed it manually.
Vet treatment cost is unpublished — nobody in the scanned threads gave a figure.
There is no sickness notification system; check animals manually each day.

Full chain: mount an Auto-Feeding Kit on the coop, build a Silo inside its range and load hay, build a Water Tower (its link radius is much smaller than the silo's), sign the water contract with the mayor, then pick food/water type on the coop trough and flip the switch — a green light confirms a correct setup.
Hovering buildings with the hammer equipped shows linkage; a silo displays how many auto-feeders connect to it, and linking happens automatically.
The water meter is on the phone, or on the wall at the far right end past the ranch gate.
Most "auto feeder does nothing" reports trace back to a missing water contract or the water tower sitting outside link radius.
The Gigi large-egg quest needs large eggs: pet chickens daily to raise their rating and use the Angela heater. Two large eggs are needed before the delivery point appears.

Daily care needs only the trough inside the coop — animals eat and drink there before leaving in the morning (official). What an outdoor area affects is large-egg chance: chickens that roam outside in an enclosed area get the chance to lay large eggs. There is no evidence that the Gigi quest requires an outdoor trough.
The chicken coop mission has no confirmed bug — bought chickens wait in the field behind Angela's house, and documented stuck cases trace back to the missed prompt.

Coop-door delivery bug: chickens submitted at the coop door enter the stock count but vanish or get stuck inside the coop's exterior wall. Walk physically inside the coop before dropping them; if one is stuck, remove all chickens and demolish the coop to drop it out.
Check linking first: walking near the door should show a stock counter like 0/6 over the dark floor area — no counter means the coop is not linked.
No fence plus an open door lets chickens wander off for good.
Without the Angela heater/AC, chickens die from heat or cold stress.
Reloading the save sometimes respawns a vanished chicken.

Selling live animals is not implemented. The official recommendation for surplus chickens and roosters is to dispatch them with an axe, pickaxe or weapon and sell the meat. The animal must be placed on the ground first — tools do not work while carrying it (that is intended, not a bug).

One detailed profit report values an adult (10+ days) Legendary chicken at roughly 24,000C in meat (1× 9,000 meat + 2× 500 legs + 8× 1,750 breasts), with Legendary eggs at S 250 / M 375 / L 590; a second player puts an ordinary mature chicken at 5,000+C of meat. Single-source numbers — meat out-earning eggs is the corroborated direction, the figures are not.

species.name: Cow
species.summary: Confirmed on the roster with milk and meat on current-build shop shelves. Purchase price, cycle and upkeep are still unmeasured — historical Alpha prices are kept as leads only.
species.searchTags: cow bull calf cattle barn milk meat spotted food diet feed price buy sell

facts.text: Cows are named as ranch animals in official material, but no seller, price or requirement has been verified in the current build.
Three barn types with exclusive interiors exist, and livestock can be raised fully outdoors without a barn — with consequences over time.
Current-build barn capacity, cost and unlock requirements are unverified.
Each species has its own unique diet under the livestock feeding system; the cow diet has not been confirmed in the current build.
Cow Milk - Small and Cow Meat - Small appear on current-build Leafy Market shelves — the items exist; how a raised cow produces them is unmeasured.
Cow Meat - Medium retails at 672C (Basic quality, restores 42 health / 130 energy). Shop shelf price, not a ranch sell price.
Meat and milk are species-specific items.
A pregnancy mechanic for mammal animals is documented, and calves exist as the early growth stage for cows and bulls. Newborn quality probability is influenced by player luck.
The animal sickness mechanic applies to livestock generally; cow-specific treatment flow is unverified in the current build.
The same Feature Kit chain (Auto-Feeding Kit + Silo + Water Tower + water contract) is documented for barns as well as coops.
Selling live animals is not implemented; the meat path is the current disposal route.

species.name: Rabbit
species.summary: Named in official store copy as bunnies and added in the Ranching v2 notes. Diet is the only community-discussed detail, and even that is unconfirmed.
species.searchTags: rabbit bunny bunnies hutch lettuce food diet feed price buy sell

facts.text: Bunnies are named as ranch animals in official store copy; seller, price and requirements are unverified.
One player guessed rabbits eat lettuce/salad greens and that hay does not work — the official reply in that thread was cut off, so the rabbit diet stays unconfirmed.

sharedSystems.text: Auto-Feeding Kit — feeds your animals automatically.
Air Conditioning Kit — prevents animals from becoming ill by keeping them warm in winter and cool in summer.
Silos and Water Towers — supply buildings; combining Feature Kits with Silos and Water Towers automates whole-livestock feeding.
Troughs — craftable feeding stations for animals outside the barn/coop or raised fully outdoors.
Linkage system — buildings and feature kits link to each other; hover with the hammer equipped to see connections. Barn and coop doors can be opened or closed at will, with benefits and consequences.
In the current build the water contract with the mayor is required before a water tower fills, and the tower's link radius is smaller than a silo's.
